html:
Tughlugh Timur (about 1312 to 1363), khan of Moghulistan, converted to Islam around 1354, and many of his Mongol nobles followed. Moghulistan was the eastern half of the Chagatai Khanate, covering the steppes of today's southeast Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and northern Xinjiang. Its Mongols had kept to their old ways, and the Muslim Turks of the western half, Transoxiana, looked down on them.

Later Muslim histories say a Persian holy man, Sheikh Jamal al-Din, and then his son Arshad al-Din, won the khan over; one later history claims some 160,000 people converted with him. The conversion made Islam the faith of the eastern Chagatai lands and, over time, of the oasis towns of the Tarim Basin, where Buddhism still lived on in places like Turfan.

Tughlugh Timur then invaded Transoxiana in 1360 and 1361 and briefly reunited the khanate. In those campaigns a young local leader named Timur first served him, then broke away and built his own empire, the Timurid Empire. Tughlugh Timur's tomb still stands near Huocheng, in the Ili valley of Xinjiang.
